land.text: Jerusalem and the coastal plain and hills round it, taken by the First Crusade; the page gives "Capture of Jerusalem: 15 July 1099" and does not name the previous owner

predecessors.note: Predecessor named from Cliopatria: the Fatimid Caliphate shape borders the kingdom from 1099 (seed neighbours list); the pages opened do not say whose land Jerusalem was.

land.text: Acre (18 May 1291), Tyre (19 May), Sidon (June), Beirut (July): the last coastal holdings, taken by the Mamluk sultan Khalil

successors.note: The title passed to the Lusignan line (Henry II was the last ruler in the infobox); no territory of the mainland remained.

capitals.name: Jerusalem
capitals.note: Infobox "Jerusalem (1099-1187)"; the city fell on 2 October 1187; from 1229 to 1244 the page says Jerusalem "was never truly reincorporated into the kingdom, which continued to be ruled from Acre".

capitals.name: Tyre
capitals.note: Infobox "Tyre (1187-1191)": the only port left in Frankish hands after Saladin's conquest.

capitals.name: Acre (Akko)
capitals.note: Infobox "Acre (1191-1291)"; the text says the kingdom "was re-established in Acre in 1192" and Acre "remained the capital for the rest of its existence".

keyframe_review.note: About 14.8 k km2 for 1099-1110: Jerusalem and its coastal plain and hills (Judaean core). The page (infobox) gives "Capture of Jerusalem: 15 July 1099" and no area figure (only population: 250,000 in 1131 and 480,000-650,000 in 1180), so the area could not be compared. Acre falls within the period (1104) and Beirut in 1110: the ledger carries those gains.

correction.text: Cliopatria 1111 shape without Transjordan (Oultrejordain) until the 1115 expedition; Beirut and Sidon included

keyframe_review.note: Cliopatria draws the 36.9 k km2 shape with the Negev and Gulf of Aqaba arm from 1111; the Oultrejordain page dates only the expedition across the Jordan to 1115 ("Baldwin ... built [Montreal] in 1115"), so Transjordan is removed for 1111-1114 and returns by the 1115 gain event. Beirut (1110), Sidon (1111) and the Galilee coast are inside the shape.

53.9 k km2 (the maximum): coastal strip from Beirut to the Gulf of Aqaba and Oultrejordain (Pagan the Butler created lord in 1126, Kerak built 1142), Tyre since 1124. The shape does not contain Ascalon, which the page gives as captured in 1153 and added to the County of Jaffa; the 1153 ledger event adds it inside this period.

union.text: Oultrejordain: "Transjordan extended southwards through the Negev to the Gulf of Aqaba"

correction.text: Cliopatria 1169 shape plus Oultrejordain (Transjordan to the Gulf of Aqaba), held until Saladin took it in 1187-1189

keyframe_review.note: Cliopatria shrinks the kingdom to 19 k km2 in 1169 and leaves out Transjordan (Aqaba, Kerak, Petra do not fall inside it), yet the Oultrejordain page has the lordship in Christian hands until Saladin took it: "invasion of the kingdom by Saladin in 1187", "By 1189 Saladin had taken all of Transjordan and destroyed its castles". The shape is kept for the west bank and Transjordan is added back for 1169-1187.

union.text: Oultrejordain: "Transjordan extended southwards through the Negev to the Gulf of Aqaba"

correction.text: Tyre and its hinterland, plus the Transjordan castles still holding out in 1188

keyframe_review.note: Cliopatria 1188-1191 is a 2.6 k km2 shape around Tyre ("Only the port of Tyre remained in Frankish hands", Kingdom page). Transjordan is added for 1188 only because the Oultrejordain page has Saladin taking "all of Transjordan" "by 1189" (loss event 1189).

8.9 k km2 for 1192-1235: the Tyre-to-Jaffa coast. "the Christians would hold the coast from Tyre to Jaffa"; "Jerusalem would remain under Islamic control" (the shape correctly leaves Jerusalem out). The 1229 gain of Jerusalem and the corridor to the coast (Sixth Crusade page) falls inside this period and is in the ledger.

8.9 k km2, practically the 1192 shape. It does not show the 1240 recovery (Theobald of Navarre's treaty "restored Jerusalem to Christian control, as well as much of the rest of the former kingdom"), the 1244 loss of Jerusalem or the 1247 Ayyubid reoccupation; the ledger carries them (1239, 1240, 1244, 1247). The extent of the 1240 recovery is unverified: page budget (the Barons' Crusade page was not opened).

correction.text: unchanged Cliopatria shape for 1260-1264; the 1265, 1266 and 1268 ledger losses reduce it to the 1272 shape

keyframe_review.note: Cliopatria keeps the 1192 coast (8.7 k km2) through 1271, but "In 1265, Baibars took Caesarea, Haifa and Arsuf, and Safad and Toron in 1266", and "In 1268 he captured Jaffa and Beaufort". The shape is right for 1260-1264 and the ledger events of 1265, 1266 and 1268 remove the lost lands until the 1272 shape takes over.

2.1 k km2 for 1272-1284: Acre, Tyre, Sidon and Beirut after the Mamluk conquests; "Edward could do nothing except arrange a ten-year truce with Baibars" (1272). The Siege of Acre page adds that "Qalawun concluded a ten-year truce with the Kingdom of Jerusalem in 1284".

The 2.1 k km2 shape is right for 1285-1291, but Cliopatria runs it to 1293 while the kingdom ended in 1291 ("Fall of Acre: 18 May 1291"; Tyre the next day; Sidon in June, Beirut in July). Years 1292-1293 should not be drawn as kingdom land; the dissolve event hands the land to the Mamluks. [orchestrator 2 Nov 2026: from/to set to 1285..1291 from this entry's own 'valid 1285-1291 only'; without them the compiler drew the shape for all its Cliopatria years, overlapping the next keyframe (window p1100-p1199 report)]

region.text: Jerusalem, Jaffa and the Judaean hills (Cliopatria 1099 shape)

ledger.note: 1099: the First Crusade takes Jerusalem (15 July) and a council in the Church of the Holy Sepulchre (22 July) founds the kingdom under Godfrey of Bouillon. Infobox "Capture of Jerusalem: 15 July 1099"; "On 22 July a council was held in the Church of the Holy Sepulchre to establish a king"; Godfrey took the title Advocatus Sancti Sepulchri. The page gives Jerusalem, not a boundary; the core is Cliopatria's 1099 shape.

1100: after Godfrey's death Baldwin I is crowned at Bethlehem and claims the title "King of the Latins of Jerusalem"; the advocacy becomes a kingdom. The page gives the title and "Daimbert compromised by crowning Baldwin in Bethlehem rather than Jerusalem"; the year follows from Godfrey dying in 1100.

1104: Baldwin I takes the port of Acre. "Baldwin captured the port cities of Acre (1104), Beirut (1110), and Sidon (1111)." The page does not name the previous owner; the Fatimid Caliphate is the counterpart Cliopatria's neighbours list gives.

1109: Tripoli falls on 12 July and Bertrand holds the south of its land as Baldwin I's vassal. "Baldwin's partition gave William the north (under Tancred) and Bertrand the south as Baldwin's vassal"; infobox "Status: Vassal of the Kingdom of Jerusalem, the Principality of Antioch and the Mongol Empire"; the county owed "fealty and homage to Baldwin I".
1110: Baldwin I takes Beirut ("Beirut (1110)"). Previous owner not named on the page.

December 1110: Baldwin I takes Sidon from the Fatimids. Siege of Sidon page: siege "19 October - 5 December 1110", "The city fell after 47 days", Sidon "had been re-fortified by the Fatimids in 1098". The Kingdom page's summary sentence gives "Sidon (1111)". [Reviewer me-09-c, 2026-10-25: re-dated from 1111 to December 1110 and re-sourced to the siege page; matches fatimid-caliphate /ledger/53.]

region.text: Oultrejordain: "Transjordan extended southwards through the Negev to the Gulf of Aqaba"

ledger.note: 1115: Baldwin I crosses the Jordan and builds Montreal; the lordship of Oultrejordain follows. "Baldwin built [Montreal] in 1115 to control the Muslim caravan routes"; Kingdom page "after his expedition across the Jordan in 1115"; "Transjordan extended southwards through the Negev to the Gulf of Aqaba". The page names no previous owner and says the eastern side "had no real borders". Cliopatria draws the Aqaba arm from 1111.

region.text: the Principality of Antioch under the regency of Baldwin II

ledger.note: 1119: after Ager Sanguinis Baldwin II takes over Antioch. "Antioch then became a vassal of Jerusalem, with Baldwin II as regent until 1126."

1124: Tyre is captured, the year of the Pactum Warmundi with Venice. "the first commercial treaty with the Republic of Venice, the Pactum Warmundi, in 1124" ... "led to the capture of Tyre that year." Previous owner not named on the page.
1126: Bohemond II arrives and rules Antioch himself; Baldwin II's regency "until 1126" ends.

region.text: the fortress of Ascalon, added to the County of Jaffa

ledger.note: 1153: Baldwin III takes Ascalon, the last Fatimid fortress on the Palestinian coast. "In 1153 Baldwin launched an offensive against Ascalon. The fortress was captured and was added to the County of Jaffa."

region.text: Egypt paying tribute to Jerusalem (Fatimid Egypt)

ledger.note: 1153: with Ascalon gone, Egypt becomes a tributary of Jerusalem. "Egypt ... was reduced to a tributary state" after Ascalon's capture; the page gives no separate year for the tribute, so it is dated to the Ascalon sentence.

region.text: refusal to pay tribute to Jerusalem

ledger.note: 1163: Egypt stops paying and Amalric invades. "In 1163 the chaotic situation in Egypt led to a refusal to pay tribute to Jerusalem"; Amalric "invaded Egypt but was turned back when the Egyptians flooded the Nile at Bilbeis". Further campaigns 1167-1169 (Bilbeis pillaged in 1168).
1164: Nur ad-Din takes Banias after Harim (12 August). "He later besieged and captured Banias." The page does not give a separate date; the Kingdom page has no entry for it.

region.text: the whole kingdom west of the Jordan except Tyre

ledger.note: 1187: Hattin (4 July) destroys the kingdom's army and Saladin takes Jerusalem on 2 October; only Tyre holds out. "On 4 July 1187, the army of the kingdom was utterly destroyed at the Battle of Hattin"; "Saladin easily overran the entire kingdom"; "Only the port of Tyre remained in Frankish hands"; infobox "First Fall of Jerusalem: 2 October 1187". Transjordan was taken later (1189).
1187: the seat of the kingdom passes from Jerusalem to Tyre. Infobox "Jerusalem (1099-1187), Tyre (1187-1191)".

region.text: Oultrejordain: "Transjordan extended southwards through the Negev to the Gulf of Aqaba"

ledger.note: 1189: Saladin takes the Transjordan castles. "By 1189 Saladin had taken all of Transjordan and destroyed its castles." The page gives "by 1189", not a month.

region.text: the coast round Acre and Jaffa fought over in the Third Crusade

ledger.note: 1189: Guy of Lusignan besieges Acre and the Third Crusade follows. "[Guy] began to besiege Acre in 1189"; the siege "lasted until 1191". The coast between Acre and Jaffa is fought over until the 1192 treaty.

1191: Acre falls to the crusaders after the long siege and becomes the capital. "During the lengthy siege, which lasted until 1191"; infobox "Acre (1191-1291)". The page gives no day or month for the recapture.
1191: the capital moves to Acre. Infobox "Acre (1191-1291)"; the text says "re-established in Acre in 1192".

region.text: the coast round Acre and Jaffa

ledger.note: 1192: the Treaty of Ramla ends the Third Crusade. "It was signed on 1 or 2 September 1192" with "a three-year truce between the two armies".

region.text: the coast from Tyre to Jaffa

ledger.note: 1192: the kingdom is restored as the coast from Tyre to Jaffa. "the Christians would hold the coast from Tyre to Jaffa"; "Jerusalem would remain under Islamic control" and Ascalon's "fortifications were to be demolished and the town returned to Saladin".

region.text: Jerusalem, Bethlehem, Nazareth, "a narrow corridor to the coast", Jaffa and Toron (part of the Sidon district)

ledger.note: 1229: the Treaty of Jaffa gives Frederick II Jerusalem and a corridor to the coast. "The treaty was concluded on 18 February 1229, and also involved a ten-year truce"; "Frederick also received Bethlehem and Nazareth, part of Sidon district, and Jaffa and Toron"; "The Muslims retained control over the Temple Mount area". Kingdom page: Jerusalem "was never truly reincorporated into the kingdom, which continued to be ruled from Acre". [Reviewer me-09-c, 2026-10-25: confidence 2: the page names no Ramla; Ramla stands in for "a narrow corridor to the coast".]
1239: the truce expires and Jerusalem is lost again. "Dawud took advantage of the Ayyubid victory to recapture Jerusalem in December, the ten-year truce having expired."

region.text: Jerusalem "as well as much of the rest of the former kingdom" (the pre-1187 land not already held on the coast)

ledger.note: 1240: Theobald of Navarre's treaty with Isma'il restores Jerusalem and more. "territorial concessions that restored Jerusalem to Christian control, as well as much of the rest of the former kingdom, even more territory than Frederick had recovered in 1229"; Ayyub "confirmed Isma'il's concessions in 1241". The page does not list the lands; the region is the pre-1187 kingdom west of the Jordan (the 1175 shape).

1244: the Khwarazmians sack Jerusalem. "With Ayyub's support, they sacked Jerusalem in the summer of 1244"; infobox "Second Fall of Jerusalem: 15 July 1244"; "On October 17 the Egyptian-Khwarazmian army destroyed the Frankish-Syrian coalition".

region.text: "most of the territory that had been conceded in 1239"

ledger.note: 1247: the Ayyubids retake what the 1239-1241 treaties conceded. "By 1247, Ayyub had reoccupied most of the territory that had been conceded in 1239." The page does not list the places.
1265: Baibars takes Caesarea, Haifa and Arsuf. "In 1265, Baibars took Caesarea, Haifa and Arsuf".
1266: Baibars takes Safad and Toron. "and Safad and Toron in 1266".
1268: Baibars takes Jaffa and Beaufort. "In 1268 he captured Jaffa and Beaufort, and then besieged and destroyed Antioch."
1289: Qalawun conquers Tripoli (26 or 27 April) and the county ends. Infobox "Conquered by Qalawun: 27 April 1289"; the Siege of Tripoli page says the Mamluks "captured the city on 26 April".

1291: Acre falls on 18 May. "The siege began on 4 April - 18 May 1291"; "By the night of 18 May, Acre was in Mamluk hands, except for the seaside Templar fortress"; Sultan Khalil "arrived at Acre on 6 April 1291".
1291: Tyre falls the next day. "Tyre fell without a fight the next day."
1291: Sidon falls in June. "Sidon fell in June".
1291: Beirut falls in July. "and Beirut in July."

region.text: the kingdom's last land, Acre, Tyre, Sidon and Beirut

ledger.note: 1291: the Kingdom of Jerusalem ends with the loss of its last cities. Infobox "Fall of Acre: 18 May 1291"; Henry II is the last ruler. The dissolve is placed at the last city, Beirut (July).

wars.name: Crusader invasions of Egypt
wars.outcome: Amalric was turned back at Bilbeis in 1163 and pillaged Bilbeis in 1168 without lasting gains; a Byzantine fleet of some 300 ships came to help him in 1169. No ground was held on the page.
wars.note: Quotes: "Amalric invaded Egypt but was turned back when the Egyptians flooded the Nile at Bilbeis"; "in 1168 Amalric pillaged Bilbeis without waiting for the naval support promised by Manuel". Zones empty because no page-dated ground was held.

wars.name: Battle of Hattin and Saladin's conquest of the kingdom

zones.text: the kingdom west of the Jordan
Oultrejordain: "Transjordan extended southwards through the Negev to the Gulf of Aqaba"

wars.outcome: Hattin (4 July 1187) destroyed the army; Jerusalem fell on 2 October 1187; "Only the port of Tyre remained in Frankish hands"; Transjordan was taken by 1189.

wars.name: Third Crusade

zones.text: the coast from Acre to Jaffa

wars.outcome: Acre recovered in 1191 after a siege begun in 1189; Richard defeated Saladin at Arsuf in 1191 and at Jaffa in 1192; the Treaty of Ramla (1 or 2 September 1192) left the Christians the coast from Tyre to Jaffa and a three-year truce.
wars.note: The Third Crusade article was not opened; the Kingdom of Jerusalem page gives "recovering most of the coast, but could not recover Jerusalem or any of the inland territory".

wars.name: Sixth Crusade

zones.text: Jerusalem, Bethlehem, Nazareth and the corridor to the coast

wars.outcome: Frederick II regained Jerusalem, Bethlehem, Nazareth, Jaffa and Toron by the treaty of 18 February 1229 with a ten-year truce, without a battle; the Temple Mount stayed Muslim.

wars.name: War of the Lombards
wars.outcome: A civil war among the kingdom's nobility sparked by Frederick II's presence; "The Lombard War was over, but the king was still absent" (1243). No territorial change.

wars.name: Barons' Crusade

zones.text: Jerusalem and much of the rest of the former kingdom

wars.outcome: Theobald's treaty with Isma'il (1240) restored Jerusalem "as well as much of the rest of the former kingdom"; Richard of Cornwall rebuilt Ascalon and Ayyub confirmed the concessions in 1241; Ayyub reoccupied most of it by 1247.
wars.note: The crusade article was not opened; the 1239 start follows from the ten-year truce of 18 February 1229 expiring (Sixth Crusade page).

wars.name: Khwarazmian sack of Jerusalem
wars.outcome: The Khwarazmians, with Ayyub's support, sacked Jerusalem in summer 1244 and on 17 October the Egyptian-Khwarazmian army destroyed the Frankish-Syrian coalition (La Forbie, not named on the page).

wars.name: War of Saint Sabas
wars.outcome: Venice and Genoa fought in Acre; Venice won the naval battle and the Genoese had to leave their quarter (1258). No territorial change for the kingdom.

wars.name: Mamluk conquests under Baibars

zones.text: Caesarea, Haifa, Arsuf, Safad, Toron, Jaffa and Beaufort

wars.outcome: Baibars took Caesarea, Haifa and Arsuf (1265), Safad and Toron (1266), Jaffa and Beaufort (1268); Edward arranged a ten-year truce in 1272.

wars.name: Fall of Acre (1291)

zones.text: the last coastal land of the kingdom

wars.outcome: Tripoli fell to Qalawun in 1289; Acre fell on 18 May 1291 after a siege begun 4 April; Tyre the next day, Sidon in June, Beirut in July; Qalawun's ten-year truce of 1284 had been dissolved by his successor.

certainty.note: Frontiers with the Muslim neighbours were fought over and never surveyed; "the eastern side had no real borders" in Oultrejordain.
Fixed by treaties: the Tyre-to-Jaffa coast of 1192, the 1229 Jaffa treaty, the truces of 1272 and 1284; inland edges stay approximate and the 1229-1247 Jerusalem corridor is a narrow treaty strip.

notes: Kingdom of Jerusalem. Five pages opened (budget 5); three more, opened for the Tripoli and Antioch dossiers of this batch, are cited for the vassal events and the 1164 Banias loss. Cliopatria ends the last shape in 1293; the kingdom ended in 1291 (Acre 18 May, Tyre 19 May, Sidon June, Beirut July): do not draw 1292-1293. Unverified (page budget): the lands of the 1240-1241 recovery and the 1247 reoccupation (the page says only Jerusalem "as well as much of the rest of the former kingdom"; the ledger uses the 1175 shape minus the coast as a stand-in, confidence 2); the Third Crusade article and the Barons' Crusade article were not opened; the exact day of the recapture of Acre (July 1191) is not on the pages. The pages opened do not name the previous owner of Acre (1104), Beirut (1110), Sidon (1111), Tyre (1124): the Fatimid Caliphate is used as counterpart because Cliopatria's Fatimid shape borders the kingdom 1099-1168 (confidence 2). Whether the Transjordan land of 1115 was stateless is not on the page (counterpart nobody). No ruler list is on the page (only Godfrey 1099-1100 and Henry II 1285-1291 in the infobox), so identity.rulers is omitted; the kings are a gap for a later pass. Suzerainty over Tripoli and Antioch: the Kingdom page says the kingdom had "suzerainty over Tripoli and Antioch" and that Baldwin I exerted "his suzerainty over the other Crusader states to the north", with no years; see the vassal events (Tripoli 1109-1289 and Antioch 1119-1126 from the County of Tripoli and Principality of Antioch pages, opened for those dossiers; Tripoli's infobox also lists it as a vassal of Antioch, undated). The Kingdom page gives the capital years Jerusalem 1099-1187, Tyre 1187-1191, Acre 1191-1291 in the infobox and "re-established in Acre in 1192" in the text. Gazetteer names needed: Ascalon (Ashkelon), Safed, Arsuf, Beaufort Castle (Arnun), Banias and Toron (Tibnin; the name Toron resolves to Toronto in the gazetteer, so coordinates are used for Toron and Banias). The Kingdom page lists no area, so the keyframe areas could not be compared with an infobox figure.
